# Brief: Condition Tracks

**Status:** Done
**Opened:** (fill date)
**Reviewer:** ChatGPT (Codex)

## Goal

Give characters five lightweight 0–3 Condition Tracks — Health, Wakefulness, Composure, Decorum, Concealment — so pressure, failure, and consequence can be modeled without a Guard, armor, inventory, or combat subsystem. 3 is strong; 0 triggers a meaningful fictional consequence; no track can kill a player character; failure changes the situation but never blocks campaign progress. Only tracks relevant to the current scene are pressured.

## Relevant canon

- Glamour is visual light-field/holographic technology, not generic spellcasting. Fabulous Glamour's modifiers must not imply spellcasting.
- The five initial outfits exist (Common Clothes, Dark Outfit, Formal Court Attire, Fabulous Glamour, Vest Inside-Out); Common Clothes is the Example Character's current Outfit.
- Reputation Markers already exist. Decorum 0 may create an appropriate existing marker such as Unsightly or Disrespectful. No new marker enum values in this pass.
- No Guard, armor points, damage absorption, protective equipment, temporary hit points, death rules, or combat-specific tracks.

## Files touched

- /Change Requests/Condition Tracks.change-request.md — this brief
- /file-types/character/schema.json — add stored `conditionState` + computed `conditionTracks`
- /file-types/character/layout.json — add a read-only Condition Tracks card near the Outfit card
- /Characters/Example Character.character.json — add stored `conditionState` (all five tracks Maximum 3, Depletion 0)
- /file-types/outfit/schema.json — add `conditionModifiers` + computed `conditionModifierRows`
- /file-types/outfit/layout.json — add a read-only Condition Modifiers card
- /Outfits/Common Clothes.outfit.json — no modifiers
- /Outfits/Dark Outfit.outfit.json — concealment +1
- /Outfits/Formal Court Attire.outfit.json — decorum +1
- /Outfits/Fabulous Glamour.outfit.json — decorum +2, concealment −2
- /Outfits/Vest Inside-Out.outfit.json — concealment +1, decorum −1
- /GM Instructions/System Rules.gm-instructions.md — add a Condition Tracks section

## Changes

- [x] **Character schema — stored state.** Add optional `conditionState` object with exactly five named properties: `health`, `wakefulness`, `composure`, `decorum`, `concealment`. Each track: `maximum` (number, enum [0, 1, 2, 3], min 0, max 3, default 3 — "the currently applicable Effective Maximum after outfit, environmental, and situational modifiers") and `depletion` (number, enum [0, 1, 2, 3], min 0, max 3, default 0 — "accumulated damage, fatigue, strain, embarrassment, or exposure that remains when Maximum changes"). Optional so minor NPCs are not forced to carry full track state; missing values compute as Maximum 3, Depletion 0.
- [x] **Character schema — computed tracks.** Add top-level computed `conditionTracks` array via ONE expression over a fixed five-row definition. Each row: stable `key`, player-facing `name`, `family` (`persistent` | `scene`), `maximum = clamp(stored maximum or 3, 0, 3)`, `depletion = clamp(stored depletion or 0, 0, 3)`, derived `current = clamp(maximum − depletion, 0, 3)`. Not in `required`; computed values never written into Character files.
- [x] **Character migration.** Example Character: add all five tracks at Maximum 3 / Depletion 0. Preserve Common Clothes as current Outfit, the image, and all existing content (Origin, Abilities, Attributes, Grace/Reputation/Species/Archetype/Lore state where present). Do not invent injuries, fatigue, embarrassment, or exposure. Minor NPCs may omit `conditionState`.
- [x] **Character layout.** Add a compact read-only Condition Tracks card near the Outfit card: repeated rows showing track name, Current, Effective Maximum (compact display-only row — track-name text plus a Current / Effective Maximum stat pair; no stepper, no editable controls), plus the caption "3 is strong. Reaching 0 triggers a consequence." No editable Maximum or Depletion controls — the AI GM updates stored state. Retain the Outfit selector; do not restore Inventory, Equipment, carrying capacity, or weight; do not expose Character Notes or Secrets; do not rebuild unrelated sections. Final schema first, then rewrite and read back the custom Character layout last.
- [x] **Outfit schema.** Add optional `conditionModifiers` array; each row REQUIRES `track` (enum: health, wakefulness, composure, decorum, concealment), `amount` (number, enum [−3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3], min −3, max +3), `appliesWhen` (prose explaining the fictional circumstances). Definition rows only — they do not directly alter stored Character Current or Depletion. The AI GM decides whether `appliesWhen` holds, combines applicable modifiers with Base Maximum 3, clamps to 0–3, and writes `maximum` into the Character track. No Craft expression interprets the free-text circumstances.
- [x] **Initial playtest outfit values.** Data-driven, NOT settled final balance: Common Clothes — none. Dark Outfit — concealment +1 (darkness, shadow, nighttime infiltration, or other situations where dark clothing plausibly helps). Formal Court Attire — decorum +1 (court, formal events, settings where formal dress is appropriate). Fabulous Glamour — decorum +2 (fey court, spectacle, celebration, contexts where conspicuous Glamour is admired), concealment −2 (when the visible Glamour is active and being visually inconspicuous matters). Vest Inside-Out — concealment +1 (avoiding Fey observation / Glamour-based recognition), decorum −1 (when socially observed and the inside-out vest appears improper or ridiculous).
- [x] **Outfit layout.** Extend the Outfit layout to display condition modifiers clearly and read-only: per row show affected track, signed amount, and when it applies. Common Clothes degrades gracefully with no empty Effects section. No editable definition controls in the normal player-facing layout. Preserve the Outfit name, description, neutral image fallback, and image-free content. Final Outfit schema first, then write and read back its custom layout.
- [x] **GM Instructions.** Add a concise Condition Tracks section to System Rules: relevance (pressure only tracks that matter; Decorum is metaphorical social/aesthetic appropriateness, not cleanliness; Concealment is whether the character stays unnoticed), checks and depletion (announce threatened track / stake / consequence before a risky check; abilities affect the check but never raise Maximums; success avoids depletion; ordinary failure +1 with a complication; severe/announced failure may add 2; never more than 2 from one ordinary check; event-based depletion without a roll when no uncertainty exists; clamp 0–3), maximum changes (Base Maximum 3; apply only currently applicable modifiers; clamp 0–3; store as `maximum`; Maximum changes never change Depletion; wasted positive modifiers at the cap are intentional; a Maximum reduction may push Current to 0), zero crossing (trigger once on a NEW crossing to 0 from a new setback or newly applied modifier; never retrigger while at 0 / on read / on recalculation; consequence is a fictional event or persistent state outside the number; raising Maximum afterward does not undo it), consequences (Health 0: unconscious/incapacitated, never dead from the track alone; Wakefulness 0: falls asleep or must rest; Composure 0: panic, freezing, flight, or blurting something damaging; Decorum 0: visible humiliation or serious social failure, may create an existing Reputation Marker such as Unsightly or Disrespectful; Concealment 0: detected), failure never blocks the campaign (pursuit/bluff/capture/changed approach, rescue/capture/lost time, changed relationships), recovery and resets (Health: treatment/healing/rest; Wakefulness: sleep or equivalent; Composure: reassurance/safety/time/control; Decorum: resets for a genuinely new social situation; Concealment: resets on a genuinely new hiding/infiltration situation; existing consequences remain), and outfit changes (read modifier definitions, decide which apply, recalculate affected Maximums from Base Maximum 3, preserve every Depletion value exactly, narrate newly caused zero crossings).
- [x] **No Guard system.** Do not add Guard, armor points, damage absorption, protective equipment, temporary hit points, death rules, or combat-specific tracks. Combat is rare and not important enough to justify that subsystem.
- [x] **Image handling.** No new art is requested. After creating the Change Request and modifying files, inspect affected content for automatically generated base images or generation metadata and remove any newly created ones. Generate no replacements. Preserve legitimate pre-existing Character imagery.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Character schema stores only Maximum and Depletion per track; Current is computed and absent from stored Character content.
- [x] Missing condition state computes as Maximum 3, Depletion 0, Current 3.
- [x] Stored track Maximum/Depletion and Outfit modifier amounts validate as discrete integers via numeric enums (0–3 and −3…+3); fractional values are rejected.
- [x] Example Character ends at Common Clothes with all five tracks Maximum 3 / Depletion 0, all pre-existing content preserved.
- [x] Every Outfit modifier row validates with a recognized track key; Common Clothes has no modifiers.
- [x] Character layout shows all five computed tracks read-only with Current and Effective Maximum; Outfit layout shows modifiers read-only and hides an empty Effects section.
- [x] Character Notes and Secrets remain absent from the player-facing layout; no Inventory or Equipment fields/bindings return; no raw GM/authoring fields were regenerated into either custom layout.
- [x] GM rules document the full condition loop: relevance, threatened-track disclosure, 1–2 Depletion on failure (never >2 per ordinary check), clamped 0–3, zero-crossing consequence once, recovery/reset rules, outfit recalc preserving Depletion.
- [x] No Guard anywhere in the system.
- [x] No affected file gained an unwanted generated image; Example Character's legitimate image is preserved.
- [x] Behavioral tests pass and are documented: Maximum-and-Depletion recalc preserving Depletion; cap enforcement (0–3 for both stored values, derived Current 0–3); zero test (Maximum 1, Depletion 1 → Current 0) and Maximum-0 test (Maximum 0, Depletion 0 → Current 0) with a single-consequence rule.

---

## Done — implementation notes (filled by the workspace assistant)

### What shipped

- **Tracks:** five 0–3 Condition Tracks — Health, Wakefulness, Composure (persistent personal conditions) and Decorum, Concealment (scene-position tracks). 3 is strong; 0 triggers a consequence; no track can kill a player character; failure changes the situation and never blocks campaign progress.
- **Architecture:** stored per track = `maximum` (the currently applicable Effective Maximum after outfit/environment/situation modifiers, clamped 0–3) and `depletion` (clamped 0–3). Current is never stored — it is derived as `clamp(maximum − depletion, 0, 3)` by the computed `conditionTracks` array. Changing an outfit or circumstance may change Maximum but never Depletion.
- **Stored vs computed:** Character files store only `conditionState`. `conditionTracks` is one top-level computed array (a single expression over a fixed five-row definition: key, name, family, maximum, depletion, current). It is not in `required` and is never written into Character files. Missing `conditionState` computes as Maximum 3 / Depletion 0 / Current 3 (verified).
- **Discrete values:** the stored `maximum`/`depletion` fields (0–3) and Outfit `conditionModifiers.amount` (−3…+3) keep their number types, minimums, maximums, defaults, and descriptions, and now also carry numeric enums — `enum: [0, 1, 2, 3]` and `enum: [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3]` — so fractional values fail validation. Verified: writing Maximum 2.5 was rejected ("must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3"). Computed expressions and stored content are unchanged.
- **Persistent vs scene:** Health, Wakefulness, Composure persist between scenes until fictionally appropriate recovery. Decorum and Concealment normally reset to 0 when a genuinely new relevant social/stealth situation begins; resetting never erases consequences already created (guards remember detection, witnesses remember humiliation, Reputation Markers remain, pursuit/suspicion/capture/fallout stays in the fiction). No generic stored consequence-history system was added.
- **Outfits:** optional `conditionModifiers` array on the Outfit schema — each row requires `track` (enum of the five stable keys), `amount` (discrete integer −3…+3), `appliesWhen` (prose). These are definition rows only; the GM adjudicates `appliesWhen`, combines applicable modifiers with Base Maximum 3, clamps to 0–3, and writes the resulting `maximum` into the appropriate Character track. No Craft expression interprets the free-text circumstances. A small computed `conditionModifierRows` field derives player-facing display rows (track display name, signed amount string, appliesWhen) purely to satisfy the read-only "affected track / signed amount / when it applies" layout requirement — storage remains the raw `conditionModifiers` numbers.
- **Initial playtest outfit values (NOT settled final balance):** Common Clothes — none. Dark Outfit — concealment +1. Formal Court Attire — decorum +1. Fabulous Glamour — decorum +2, concealment −2 (Glamour remains visual light-field/holographic technology, not spellcasting). Vest Inside-Out — concealment +1, decorum −1.
- **GM rules:** added the Condition Tracks section to System Rules (placed after Outfits), covering relevance, checks and depletion, maximum changes, zero crossing and consequences, recovery and resets, and outfit changes. Also corrected the Outfits section's old "no outfit bonuses, penalties… exist yet" sentence to state that outfits may carry Condition Modifiers (the only outfit effect in v1).
- **No Guard:** no Guard, armor points, damage absorption, protective equipment, temporary hit points, death rules, or combat-specific tracks were added anywhere.
- **Character layout:** a read-only Condition Tracks card sits directly after the Outfit card — it repeats the computed `conditionTracks` array with a compact display-only row per track (track-name text plus a Current / Effective Maximum stat pair) plus the caption "3 is strong. Reaching 0 triggers a consequence." The Outfit selector is retained; no Inventory, Equipment, carrying capacity, or weight bindings; no Character Notes or Secrets exposure; no unrelated sections rebuilt. The final schema was established first, then the custom layout was written and read back (last).
- **Outfit layout:** a Condition Modifiers card (visible only when `conditionModifiers` exists, so Common Clothes shows no empty Effects section) repeats `conditionModifierRows` read-only: track name, signed amount badge, appliesWhen prose. Name, description, neutral image fallback, and image-free content preserved. Final schema first, then custom layout written and read back.
- **Migration scope:** exactly 1 Character file (Example Character) and 5 Outfit files existed; both were reconciled with the new schemas. Example Character keeps Common Clothes, its pre-existing portrait, and all prior content (Origin, Abilities, Attributes, notes, description, personality); all five tracks stored at Maximum 3 / Depletion 0. No injuries, fatigue, embarrassment, or exposure were invented.

### Validation results (behavioral tests, Example Character)

- **Maximum & Depletion test:** Concealment Maximum 2 / Depletion 1 → Current 1 ✓. Recalculated Maximum to 3 while Depletion stayed 1 → Current 2 ✓; stored Depletion was read back unchanged at 1.
- **Cap test:** writing Depletion 4 was rejected by schema validation ("must be <= 3"). Stored Maximum and Depletion are constrained 0–3; derived Current stays 0–3 via the clamp (observed across every test).
- **Discrete-value test:** after adding the numeric enums, writing Maximum 2.5 was rejected by schema validation ("must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3"). Stored track values accept only integers 0–3; Outfit `amount` accepts only integers −3…+3.
- **Zero test:** Concealment Maximum 1 / Depletion 1 → Current 0 ✓. The GM rules require exactly one consequence on the new crossing, not repeated consequences from remaining at 0, reading the file, or recalculation.
- **Maximum-0 test:** Health was temporarily set to Maximum 0 / Depletion 0; the computed `conditionTracks` row read Current 0 / Maximum 0 / Depletion 0 ✓. Rendered-layout check: the track row no longer uses Progress — see the peer-review corrections below for why — and the replacement row is display-only, so Maximum 0 renders as plain "Current 0 / Effective Maximum 0" with no bar math.
- **Missing-state test:** with `conditionState` removed, all five tracks computed Maximum 3 / Depletion 0 / Current 3 ✓.
- All temporary test state was restored afterward: Example Character wears Common Clothes; all five tracks end at Maximum 3 / Depletion 0.
- Final read-back confirmed: schemas store only Maximum + Depletion per track; `conditionTracks` and `conditionModifierRows` are computed and absent from stored content; every Outfit modifier row validates with a recognized track key; Common Clothes has no modifiers; the Character layout shows all five tracks read-only with Current and Effective Maximum; the Outfit layout is read-only and hides the empty section; no Notes/Secrets/Inventory/Equipment bindings returned; no raw GM/authoring fields were regenerated into either custom layout.

### Peer-review corrections (final pass)

- **Discrete values enforced.** Added numeric enums so fractional values cannot validate: every Character `conditionState` `maximum` and `depletion` field is now `enum: [0, 1, 2, 3]`; Outfit `conditionModifiers.amount` is now `enum: [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3]`. Number types, minimums, maximums, defaults, descriptions, computed expressions, and all stored content are unchanged. Verified: writing Maximum 2.5 was rejected ("must be one of 0, 1, 2, 3").
- **Maximum-0 layout case.** Temporarily set Health to Maximum 0 / Depletion 0; the computed `conditionTracks` row returned Current 0 / Maximum 0 / Depletion 0. The Condition Track row no longer uses Progress: a Progress bar's fill at Maximum 0 risks division-by-zero and the rendered behavior could not be visually confirmed from the tooling layer, so the row was replaced with a compact display-only presentation (track-name text + a Current / Effective Maximum stat pair) that renders Maximum 0 as plain values with no bar math. It is read-only with no stepper. The rest of the Character layout was not rebuilt.
- **Layout regeneration cleaned.** The Character schema edit re-triggered schema-to-layout regeneration that appended player-facing Notes, Secrets, and raw Condition State sections (nine elements). Those were removed again and the vetted page stack restored; the only new card is the read-only Condition Tracks card. Notes and Secrets remain absent from the player-facing layout.
- No images were generated or removed in this pass; Example Character's legitimate portrait is preserved.

### Image handling

- The platform auto-added a generated base image to this Change Request on creation despite `autoImageGeneration: false` — it was removed and no replacement was generated. No other affected file gained an image; Example Character's legitimate pre-existing portrait is preserved. (The Outfit and Character schema edits did not reintroduce images on any of the six data files.)

### Assumptions / open questions

- The initial outfit numbers are playtest values, not settled final balance — recorded as such in the brief and here.
- `amount` is typed as `number` (the platform's supported types) with minimum −3 / maximum 3 AND a numeric enum, so it enforces discrete integers in −3…+3; track `maximum`/`depletion` enforce discrete integers 0–3 the same way.
- Brief date left for the human/reviewer to fill.

## Review (filled by ChatGPT / the human after the pull)

<left for reviewer>
name: Condition Tracks
description: Adds five lightweight 0–3 Condition Tracks (Health, Wakefulness, Composure, Decorum, Concealment) with stored Maximum + Depletion and a derived Current, persistent vs scene-position families, Outfit condition modifiers, Character and Outfit layout updates, GM rules for relevance, checks, zero-crossing consequences, recovery and resets, and an explicit omission of any Guard or combat subsystem.
